## Best age by current health state

This dot plot shows participant-level points across current health states. Each dot is one filtered record from the data (First to Third doses only), so the figure contains the full set of points rather than one summary point per state.

```{python}
#| label: fig-age-health-state
#| fig-cap: "Participant-level age points by current health state"
#| echo: false

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

vax = pd.read_csv("covid_vaccination.csv", low_memory=False)
daily = pd.read_csv("covid_daily_survey.csv", low_memory=False)

daily = daily[["VSAFE_SYSTEM_ID", "HAD_SYMPTOMS"]].copy()
daily["HAD_SYMPTOMS"] = daily["HAD_SYMPTOMS"].astype(str).str.strip().str.lower()

outcome = daily.groupby("VSAFE_SYSTEM_ID").agg(
  symptom_free=("HAD_SYMPTOMS", lambda values: int((values != "yes").all()))
).reset_index()

merged = outcome.merge(
  vax[["VSAFE_SYSTEM_ID", "age_at_vax_yrs", "CURRENT_STATE", "DOSE_NUMBER"]],
  on="VSAFE_SYSTEM_ID",
  how="inner",
)

age_order = ["0.5-04", "05-11", "12-19", "20-29", "30-39", "40-49", "50-59", "60-69", "70-79", "80+"]
age_midpoints = {
  "0.5-04": 2,
  "05-11": 8,
  "12-19": 15.5,
  "20-29": 24.5,
  "30-39": 34.5,
  "40-49": 44.5,
  "50-59": 54.5,
  "60-69": 64.5,
  "70-79": 74.5,
  "80+": 85,
}
state_order = ["Excellent", "Very good", "Good", "Fair", "Poor"]

merged = merged.dropna(subset=["age_at_vax_yrs", "CURRENT_STATE", "DOSE_NUMBER"])
merged = merged[merged["age_at_vax_yrs"] != "Invalid"].copy()
merged = merged[merged["DOSE_NUMBER"].isin(["First", "Second", "Third"])].copy()
merged = merged[merged["CURRENT_STATE"].isin(state_order)].copy()

merged["age_value"] = merged["age_at_vax_yrs"].astype(str).map(age_midpoints)
merged = merged.dropna(subset=["age_value"])

state_to_x = {state: i for i, state in enumerate(state_order)}
merged["x_value"] = merged["CURRENT_STATE"].map(state_to_x)

# Add small deterministic jitter so overlapping points become visible.
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
merged["x_jitter"] = merged["x_value"] + rng.normal(0, 0.07, size=len(merged))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6))
ax.scatter(merged["x_jitter"], merged["age_value"], s=11, alpha=0.32, color="#2f6f9f", edgecolors="none")

ax.set_xlabel("Current health state")
ax.set_ylabel("Age (years)")
ax.set_title("All participant-level age points by current health state")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(state_order)))
ax.set_xticklabels(state_order)
ax.set_yticks([age_midpoints[label] for label in age_order])
ax.set_yticklabels(age_order)
plt.xticks(rotation=20, ha="right")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

This is still an exploratory visualization based on reported symptoms rather than a causal estimate of vaccine timing.
